items.text: Hi everyone, Jay and team here!
Our tech team has been busy tinkering to provide an improved online play experience for this update.
Here's the patch notes for v1.1.4; do let us know if these updates worked for your gameplay experience!

[img src="https://shared.fastly.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/2650730/extras/Divider.png?t=1747981232" style="border-width: medium; border-style: none; border-color: currentcolor; border-image: none; -webkit-user-drag: none; max-width: 100%;"]
Reworked and improved robustness to Online Play connectivity, to prevent timeouts and network disconnections from breaking the connection to EOS servers.
Clearer error message/feedback to players regarding their network connectivity status upon selecting the ‘Online Play’ button.
More informative error messages for failing to join a Lobby, such as informing if the Lobby is full.
If accepting a Steam Invite fails, an error message would be displayed as feedback.
Added a profanity filter to the generation of Lobby Codes.
Standardised the sequence of languages in the Options menu: Thai is now grouped along with the rest of the Southeast Asian languages.
Online Multiplayer
Fixed an issue where the Steam ‘Invite to Play’ feature was not working in recent versions of the game.
Fixed an issue where it was not previously possible to accept a Steam Invite from the Options, Credits, or Character Select screens.
Fixed an issue where entering a blank lobby code in the Join Game panel will cause the game to be stuck on “Connecting…”.
Fixed an issue where the Disconnect Popup in the Main Menu, after exiting a networked game session, could not be closed via mouse.
Fixed an issue where a small number of Wok, Work Table and Pot cooking minigames in the Mountains that feature two (2) juices are not reflected accurately across Networked Play.
Fixed an issue where the client (P2) playing the Squid fishing minigame does not reflect across Networked Play for the host (P1).
Fixed an issue where, if the client (P2) is playing as Som, the Cooker, and exits session, their orbs remain visible in the level.
Fixed an issue where, if the client (P2) gets hit just as they complete a fishing minigame, the fished item drops in an inaccessible area.
Fixed an issue where a monster might stop behaving as intended if the client (P2) disconnects.
Fixed an issue where, after joining another player’s Lobby and leaving it, the player does not see their own save file’s chosen Difficulty Mode in the Options menu.
Visual
Fixed an issue where an unused ring mesh can be spotted around Nagarasa.
As always, thank you for playing SEDAP! and please continue to support us!

Thank you so much for your patience -- the update that all of us have been waiting for is here!

Our team has spent the past few weeks refining and improving SEDAP! to bring you a new and improved game experience. This update tackles key player feedback received since its release in May, introducing four major highlights: an in-game map, selectable difficulty modes, new Charms, and the Bestiary!
Also, along with the update, we’ve added Steam community items! Collect trading cards, badges, profile backgrounds, and emoticons when you play SEDAP! on Steam.
Without further ado, here are the (very looong) patch notes for v1.1.
[img src="https://shared.fastly.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/2650730/extras/Divider.png?t=1747981232"]
For a quick overview of this update, you may watch this 2-minute video.
The new in-game map helps players with navigating larger levels -- a quick toggle shows an aerial view of the level, denoting player locations, and ingredient spawns with respawn timers.

Toggle the map on and off any time during a level by using "Tab" for keyboard controls, and "Left Shoulder/LB" for controllers. For local multiplayer players using a shared keyboard, the toggle button would be "V" and "," (default controls).
For players who prefer a more casual experience, Herb Mode is a new difficulty setting in the game, where damage taken, monster HP, dish freshness and order timing depletions are greatly reduced.
Players can toggle between the two modes at the start of the game, and in the game’s settings while in the Camp.
However, please note that you will only be able to earn Pink Stars in Spice Mode, the game’s standard difficulty.
Refresh your adventure with four brand new Charms and an increased Charm carry limit!
Jade Earrings: Player attacks will no longer be interrupted by incoming attacks.
Unlocked after beating 02-03
Five Stones: Prevents Combo Streak from expiring.
Unlocked after beating 02-07
Yadom: Slows the rate of food going bad by 25%.
Unlocked after beating 02-SP
Kerosang: Grants a 2x Combo Streak at the start of the level.
Unlocked after beating 03-SP
The Bestiary is a new chapter of the Makanomicon featuring brand new artwork, names, and detailed descriptions of the Monsters you’ll encounter.
Just like dishes, Bestiary pages unlock only after encountering the monsters.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44711281/ea777d271dcd806e3a8455fcc202a918038768e6.png"]

Please note that with the addition of the in-game map toggle and certain input-related bug fixes, keyboard and controller re-bindings have been reset to default to prevent overlapping bindings. We're sorry for any inconvenience!
Dakila now has new dialogue lines when purchasing from the Shop.
Merapi's Radio is now accessible from the Camp -- you may now yap with her!
General
\[Single-player] \[Standard Levels] Increased Combo Streak length (+10s)
\[Single-player] \[Spirit Trial Levels] Increased Combo Streak length (+30s)
Decreased the rate of food decay.
Increased the critical rate boost at Combo Streak x7

Revised the unlock levels for certain Weapons, Utensils, and Charms. Previously purchased equipment remains unaffected.
In light of the newly-added Charms and balancing changes, the unlock levels for Charms in the Beach and Mountains have been adjusted.
2-star Spatula and Parang can now be unlocked earlier in the game, after beating 01-05.
3-star Ngao, Sibat, Celurit and Chopsticks can now be unlocked earlier in the game, after beating 03-02.
Utensils
Decreased charging time for Utensils. The only exception to this is the Frying Pan, to allow players to check the cast range before casting.
Chopsticks
2-star now freezes all Order timers for 30 seconds
3-star charged ability now restores only 30 seconds to the Order time, but also freezes them for 30 seconds
Cleaver

Weapons

Charged ability now instantly breaks Armour

SEDAP! is currently sitting at "Mixed" reviews on Steam. This means that a significant number of our players aren’t satisfied with the game right now. We really want to change that. We love SEDAP!, and our team acknowledges that it wasn't released in its best state. From its release in May until now, we've been reading all your feedback and doing whatever we could to help.

Now that we're wrapping up console development, we can finally shift gears and focus on building SEDAP! version 1.1 - a major balancing and content update that addresses these frustrations to the best of our ability.
Soooo, in this post, I'd like to share about our console versions, and what's in store for v1.1!

As mentioned above, Version 1.1 is our response to your feedback, addressing the frustrations and challenges many players have faced, namely the late-game levels being too difficult, especially in single-player mode.
Before we dive in into what v1.1 will offer, let's first do a little recap:

notes.title: Issues that we've tackled in previous patches

items.text: 🌐 Online Multiplayer Instability

We've switched from using Epic Online Services (EOS) to Steam Game Servers. Since then, players have reported improvements in online multiplayer stability. For our players based in China, we highly recommend using an accelerator to play in online multiplayer mode.
🏆 Steam Achievements
We've fixed a bunch of bugs relating to Steam Achievements, and we also updated the game with visuals to display progress on some Achievements.
⚖️ Balancing

Balancing for the game came in bits and pieces, such as slowing down the speed of raining Fireballs and adjusting some numbers here and there. But, it's safe to say that more balancing changes will come in v1.1 and will be the biggest balancing patch yet!

notes.title: Here's what you can expect in v1.1 so far

items.text: (!) Please note that these features are still subject to change as we continue testing and refining the player experience.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44711281/31c6eda9df07b2eb19128b62cfcce80a29d36739.png"]
🌏 Minimap
This is probably the most-requested feature by our players.
This feature aims to support navigation and planning in bigger maps by providing information on ingredient spawns.
The Minimap is toggled by pressing a designated button, showing players:
(1) a top-down overview of the level
(2) the player's current location in the level
(3) the positions + estimated respawn times of ingredient spawns
☀️ Difficulty Modes
While some players are happy with the game’s current level of difficulty, many others feel that the game as it is right now is too challenging and stressful.

Currently, we're contemplating to add a "Casual Mode" to make the game more accessible to players who prefer a less challenging experience while still being able to complete the campaign. "Casual Mode" would offer the following adjustments:
(1) more time given to complete each order
(2) more time given for food to go bad
(3) reduced Monster HP + damage
(4) less intense Rush Hour
(5) infinite cooking minigame chances
The difficulty mode can be changed at any point in the campaign.
Please note that you will not be able to earn Pink Stars in "Casual Mode".
⚒️ Level Adjustments
A good chunk of player frustration was due to some awkwardly-placed elements in certain levels, particularly those from the latter half of the Beach and Mountains.
Without making mega gigachad changes to these levels, we’ve made the following adjustments to create a smoother level experience while still maintaining a fair and satisfying level of challenge.
(1) re-ordered some order sequences for single-player
(2) re-positioned some Teletotems, Kitchenware and Interactables
(3) rewired some teleporter networks for Teletotems, Whirlpools, and Wind Portals
